subject: mods to base model class to support log prob w/o Jacobian?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: mods to base model class to support log prob w/o Jacobian?
parts:
I have a question about how to extend our base model classes (used
to do the auto-diff calcs) to allow the log prob function to
be computed w/o the Jacobian adjustment.

Because we don't want to have to compile different models for
optimization and sampling, I've modified the code generator so that
there's a new boolean template parameter, jacobian, in the underlying log probability
function that is generated from a model:

template <bool propto, bool jacobian, typename T>
T log_prob_poly(vector<T>& params_r,
vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* msg_stream = 0);

The parameter jacobian controls whether or not the log Jacobian
of the constraint inverse transform is added to the log probabilty or not.

There shouldn't be any runtime overhead because it's a static if on
the template parameter.

The abstract base class for the models (it has the auto-diff code)
relies on the log_prob function over var, which I've defined to
include the Jacobian.

var log_prob(vector<var>& params_r,
vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* pstream = 0) {
return log_prob_poly<true,true,var>(params_r,params_i,pstream);
}

I also defined this:

var log_prob_no_jacobian(vector<var>& params_r,
vector<int>& params_i,
std::ostream* pstream = 0) {
return log_prob_poly<true,false,var>(params_r,params_i__,pstream);
}

Should we add that to the model along with the matching
auto-diff versions for gradients?

- Bob

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mods to base model class to support log prob w/o Jacobian?
parts:
On Friday, July 12, 2013 1:07:15 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
I can change the optimizers on the same branch to make
sure everything's still working.  I should finish it
off over the weekend.  The only thing I need to do is
template the model class in the optimizers the
same way it's templated for the samplers.

Given that there seem to be a lot of people on stan-users who really like Bayes factorish things, do you think we should have some post-sampling function to facilitate calculating the posterior density averaged over the retained draws, keeping the normalizing constants and not doing the modification due to the change-of-variables to the unbounded parameter space?

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] mods to base model class to support log prob w/o Jacobian?
parts:
Sounds good to me.

It would probably be easiest to do it post-sampling
in the retained iterations (the same way generated quantities is
done now).

It would be up to the user to make sure all the normalization terms
were included --- we could only compute what's in their function.
If they have a full model, it'd be a log density over parameters theta and
modeled data y (given unmodeled data x),

log p(y,theta|x),

not the posterior log density

log p(theta|y,x).

This would be a nice standalone project for someone to do. Preferably
after 2.0 is out, when the basic command structure's more ironed out.

- Bob
